newsitem.title: INDIA: India to clear Bangalore airport - state minister.
newsitem.headline: India to clear Bangalore airport - state minister.

text.p: A state minister said on Tuesday he was confident India's federal government would soon approve a proposal by an international consortium to build a new airport in the southern city of Bangalore.
"The project will be cleared by July," R.V. Deshpande, industries minister in the Karnataka state government, told reporters in the state capital Bangalore.
"The prime minister has given us his assurance. The state government will not allow it to be shelved, and it will be built by the Tata consortium," he said.
The consortium links India's Tata group, Raytheon Inc of the United States and Singapore's Changi Airport Authority.
The Karnataka government has already agreed to the consortium's proposal for a build-own-and-operate deal.
But Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim in New Delhi has opposed the project and wants it executed on a build-operate-and-transfer (BOT) basis.
"Definitely the statements of the minister and the delays have sent wrong signals to foreign investors," Deshpande said.
"Now everything is cleared and the project will take off after July," he said without elaborating.
